name: Baked Lentils With Cheese
directions:
Preheat oven to 375°.
                        
                        Combine in shallow 9x13" baking dish: lentils, water, bay leaf, salt, pepper, marjoram, sage, thyme, onions, garlic, and canned tomatoes.
                        
                        Cover tightly and bake for 30 minutes.
                        
                        Uncover and stir in carrots and celery.
                        
                        Bake covered for 40 minutes until vegetables are tender.
                        
                        Stir in green pepper and parsley.
                        
                        Sprinkle cheese on top.
                        
                        Bake uncovered for 5 minutes until cheese melts.

name: black beans and rice
ingredients: Two 15-ounce cans black beans, drained, or 30 ounces cooked dry beans
3 cups cooked white or brown rice
1 avocado, pitted, peeled, and chopped (optional, for serving)
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
directions:
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add half the onion, garlic, and salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is soft and translucent, about 3 minutes.
                        
                        Stir in the cumin, pepper, and oregano and cook for 1 minute more. Add the beans and water and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the beans are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon oil.
                        
                        Serve the black beans over rice, garnished with the remaining onion, the avocado (if using), and lime wedges.

name: Couscous with Chickpeas, Dates and Scallions
ingredients: 1/2 cup pitted dates, chopped OR 1/2 cup dried apricots, chopped
Kosher salt and ground black pepper
1 cup boiling water (or 1.5 cup water for quinoa)
directions:
In a large bowl, combine the couscous, chickpeas, harissa, dates, 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper.
                        
                        Stir in the boiling water, cover and let stand until absorbed, about 10 minutes.
                        
                        In a small bowl, whisk together the oil and lemon zest and juice.
                        
                        Using a fork, fluff the couscous mixture.
                        
                        Add the oil mixture and scallions, then toss.
                        
                        Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Assemble in instant pot and cook for 1 minute. Use natural release.

name: Pasta with Lentils and Thyme
ingredients: ¼ cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
Two 15-ounce cans brown lentils, rinsed and drained
8 ounces ditalini OR mezze rigatoni pasta
Kosher salt and ground black pepper
Garnish: finely grated Parmesan cheese or fresh parsley or both
directions:
In a large saucepan, heat the oil until shimmering.
                        
                        Add the garlic and cook, stirring, until fragrant.
                        
                        Stir in the tomato paste and cook until the oil turns red.
                        
                        Whisk in the wine and thyme, then cook, stirring, until the liquid has almost fully evaporated.
                        
                        Add 3 cups water, the lentils, pasta and 1 teaspoon each salt and pepper.
                        
                        Bring to a boil, then lower to simmer.
                        
                        Cook, uncovered and stirring occasionally, until the pasta is al dente.
                        
                        Season with salt and pepper.
                        
                        Serve drizzled with additional oil.

name: Pot-in-Pot Puerto Rican Rice and Beans
ingredients: 1 (15.5-ounce) can pink or red kidney beans, undrained
1 medium (5-ounce) all-purpose or russet potato, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch cubes
1/2 tablespoon sazón seasoning, homemade or store-bought
directions:
For the sofrito: In a small food processor, finely chop the onion, cubanelle, garlic, and cilantro.
                        
                        For the beans: Press the sauté button on an electric pressure cooker. When hot, add the oil and sofrito and cook, stirring, until softened, about 2 minutes. Add the beans (not drained) to the pot, along with 3/4 cup water, the tomato sauce, potato, sazón, bay leaf, oregano, salt, and black pepper to taste.
                        
                        For the rice: In a heatproof bowl that will fit in the pressure cooker, stir together 1/4 cups water, the rice, and salt. Place the steaming rack/trivet over the beans, then place the bowl on top of the rack.
                        
                        Seal and cook on high pressure for 12 minutes, until the rice is cooked and can easily be fluffed with a fork. Natural release for 10 minutes.
                        
                        Carefully take the bowl of rice out of the pressure cooker and fluff with a fork. Remove the rack from the pressure cooker. Discard the bay leaf and serve the beans over the rice, topped with the avocado, tomato, and hot sauce, if desired.

name: Spanish Chickpeas and Rice
ingredients: 1 cup uncooked long grain white rice
directions:
Mince garlic and add to sauté pan with olive oil. Cook over medium-low heat for 1-2 minutes, or just until soft and fragrant. Add spices, then stir and sauté with hot oil for 1 minute.
                        
                        Dice the onion and add, sautéing until soft and translucent for about 5 minutes. Add the rice and sauté for 2 minutes more.
                        
                        Drain the chickpeas and artichoke hearts and add to the skillet with the diced tomatoes, broth, and salt. Roughly chop the parsley and add, saving a small amount to sprinkle before serving. Stir until combined.
                        
                        Place a lid on the skillet and turn heat up to medium-high, allowing the skillet to come to a boil. When it reaches a boil, reduce heat to low and make sure it actively simmers for 20 minutes.
                        
                        After simmering for 20 minutes, turn heat off and allow the skillet to rest for 5 minutes without removing the lid. Remove the lid, fluff with a fork, top with the remaining parsley. Cut the lemon into wedges and squeeze fresh juice over each bowl.
